Short deleted group after propres has a descending crossing and a small loop, but the thick strike masks the letter bodies; sp. is plausible, de cannot be excluded.
Looped d, separate apostrophe and joined low un occur immediately before the terminal capital.
Terminal capital has a strong diagonal/vertical junction and two looped compartments crossed by a long line; this suggests B but does not securely exclude a overwritten A.
Crossed-out label preserves the slanted N, small raised circle, and 5 with upper horizontal stroke and lower curved return.
Number before Compléments is overwritten: a closed lower loop of 6 survives beneath a hooked upper correction compatible with 5; the layers cannot be separated confidently.
Between L and inégalité a dense horizontal deletion covers the letter body; no recoverable counter distinguishes a from another cancelled beginning.
At the right end of the cancelled line the o, descending p, elevated acute and tall t survive the strike, with a linked eurs ending.
Insertion above the lower deleted clause has a descending f, d ascender, elongated middle connection and crossed t with final ale curve; the strokes support the proposed singular form.
Cancelled short insertion before AB retains a tall descending p and a low linked our sequence above the strike.
